blind_spots.blind_spot: 'to hand off tracking to other UAV feeds' assumes a live inter-platform data link
blind_spots.operator_reality: DDIL contested environments deny the continuous bandwidth needed to hand off a tracked target between UAV feeds in real time — same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case, just at the platform-to-platform level instead of platform-to-ground
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the abstract frames this purely as an algorithmic capability ('automatically... hand off tracking'), not as a comms-constrained operation
blind_spots.evidence_quote: to hand off tracking to other UAV feeds, or to automatically search through vast amounts of archived feeds captured by persistent ISR, to provide decision quality results

blind_spots.blind_spot: no ATO/RMF/IL4-5 language despite pursuing a $25M sole-source AF contract to run software against ISR video feeds
blind_spots.operator_reality: software touching AF ISR data on government networks needs an Authority to Operate and STIG compliance before it can move past a program-office pilot; a 2-4 person team with zero visible compliance hires is exactly the profile that stalls at this gate
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: site and abstracts are written entirely in technical-superiority language (accuracy vs. Neural Nets) with no fielding/compliance section
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ZAC was awarded $25M contract from US Air force (Feb 2026).

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'human-level Situational Awareness' claims with no mention of the human who uses it
blind_spots.operator_reality: an ISR analyst or sensor operator has to be trained to trust, verify, and act on ZAC's automated tracking output; without CONOPS or training-and-sustainment language, the tool risks being a lab demo that never gets adopted into an actual watch-floor workflow
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the entire narrative is AGI/company-of-global-consequence framing aimed at investors and press, not at the operator who would run ZAC Locator/Describer day to day
blind_spots.evidence_quote: enables powerful human-level Situational Awareness, e.g., with applications in autonomy and actionable monitoring

opener_hook: ZAC's $25M sole-source Air Force contract (announced March 2026) follows two 2022 Phase II SBIRs with the MQ-9 program office — built and run by a team of 2-4 people.
what_they_do: Few-shot, explainable 3D image-recognition AI (CXAI) for tracking passenger vehicles in MQ-9 aerial ISR video, now under a $25M sole-source Air Force contract.
